GLEUHR – Branch Manager Responsibilities & Process Guidelines
Consolidated reference | September–October 2026 | Timings revised 26 October 2026: BM on duty 9:30 AM to 7:00 PM | POCs and 24-hour call rule added 27 October 2026
BM working hours: 9:30 AM to 7:00 PM
The Branch Manager is on duty from 9:30 AM to 7:00 PM. Every daily BM task in these guidelines is done inside those hours, in the order below. The FDM (or the senior receptionist where there is no FDM) readies the branch before 9:30 AM and runs it after 7:00 PM.
Time
What the BM does
9:30 – 9:45 AM
Clinic opens. Confirm every room is ready; check attendance, late arrivals and grooming. Share the opening photo and confirmation by 9:45 AM.
9:45 – 10:05 AM
Morning briefing: reception (5 min), housekeeping (5 min), counsellors (10 min), one station at a time. Assign duties and confirm them in the WhatsApp group. Share morning staff and cleanliness photos.
10:05 – 10:25 AM
BM-Doctor meeting. MoM filed the same day.
10:25 – 11:00 AM
Read yesterday's numbers and the FDM debrief. Morning physical stock check. Acknowledge HQ emails. Plan the day.
11:00 AM – 6:00 PM
Branch walks at 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM. Photo rounds every 2 hours (11:30, 1:30, 3:30, 5:30). Observe consultations; keep CRM, Airtable and prescriptions current; update the Issue Tracker; check machines and CCTV; handle complaints, stock and petty cash.
6:00 – 6:15 PM
Counsellor debrief.
6:15 – 6:30 PM
Fill the BM Daily Log, BM EOD report and stock report. Make owed callbacks.
6:30 – 6:45 PM
Cash cut-off: reconcile Cash, Card and UPI for billing up to 6:30 PM and explain variances. Washroom checklist photo.
6:45 – 6:55 PM
Team close: thank 2–3 people by name.
6:55 – 7:00 PM
Submit the reports, send the WhatsApp summary to the RH, and leave a handover note for the FDM. BM off duty at 7:00 PM.
After 7:00 PM the FDM reconciles billing taken after the 6:30 PM cut-off, seals it with a signed slip, completes the closing audit with housekeeping and sends the FDM debrief by 8:00 PM. The BM checks the slip and the debrief at 9:30 AM the next morning. Patient-safety, security or major cash issues after 7:00 PM are phoned to the BM at once and escalated to the RH.
Points of contact (POC) and email communication
Every concern has one owner at HQ. Email that POC and copy every other POC the issue touches. Email is the record: a call or WhatsApp message can alert someone, but it does not replace the email.

Email rules
All communication with HQ POCs is on email. Address the POC who owns the issue, and copy every related POC and your RH.
If an issue touches two areas, keep both POCs in the loop. Example: a machine breakdown that delays booked treatments goes to Saurabh with Dr Navreet copied; a stock shortage that stops a treatment goes to Aditya with Saurabh and Dr Navreet copied.
Zoho Inventory ID, password or stock discrepancy issues go to Aditya.
Subject line: [Branch] · [Area] · [Short issue] · [Date]. In the body: what happened, the client or item affected, what you have done, what you need and by when.
Urgent patient-safety, security or major cash issues may be phoned first, but must be confirmed on email the same day.
Log the issue in the Issue Tracker with the email date, and keep replying on the same email thread until it is closed with evidence.
Client calls within 24 hours of every visit
Every client gets two calls within 24 hours of every visit: one from the doctor and one from the Feedback Team. Both calls depend on the details the branch enters in the system (CRM / Airtable). A wrong number or a missing visit means a client nobody calls, so every visit must be entered correctly, without a miss.
Enter every visit on the same day, before the client leaves: client name, mobile number, treatment or service done and session number, treating doctor and therapist, any concern or reaction, and the next appointment.
Read the mobile number back to the client and correct it on the spot. Never leave it blank or enter a placeholder number.
Keep the visit status correct (Visit Done, No Show, Cancelled, Rescheduled) so the right clients are called.
At 6:15 PM, before the daily reports, the BM checks that every visit of the day is in the system and complete. Gaps are fixed before 7:00 PM.
If the doctor or the Feedback Team report a client they could not reach because of wrong or missing details, correct it the same day and record it as a missed entry in the BM Daily Log.
1. Daily branch opening and operational readiness
Ensure the clinic opens on time at 9:30 AM, the start of the BM shift (9:30 AM to 7:00 PM).
Share the clinic opening photo and confirmation by 9:45 AM.
Ensure all staff report on time and attendance is marked correctly.
Report late arrivals and reasons for delay.
Share morning photos of Reception and Housekeeping staff.
Ensure staff follow the prescribed dress code, formal attire, and badge requirements; round-neck T-shirts are not permitted.
Conduct the morning briefing and assign duties to the concerned staff.
Share confirmation of assigned duties in the designated WhatsApp group.
Ensure all rooms and clinic areas are ready before patient operations begin.
Follow the maximum occupancy instruction of four people in the lift.
2. Clinic hygiene, housekeeping and photographs
Share morning cleanliness photos of every clinic area.
Ensure a complete clinic round with photos of every area every two hours.
Check Reception, treatment rooms, doctors’ cabins, washrooms, waiting areas, balconies, and other applicable spaces.
Ensure medical stock and consumables are stored hygienically and are not left open or exposed.
Complete and share the washroom checklist photo at day-end.
Maintain a weekly deep-cleaning schedule.
Ensure Housekeeping responsibilities are assigned and monitored.
Report and resolve hygiene gaps immediately, with evidence of closure.
3. Daily stock management and consumption reporting
Update the branch stock sheet daily without missing any entry.
Complete the morning physical stock check and confirm that the count matches the recorded stock.
Report any stock mismatch immediately to the concerned RH and Operations Team.
Maintain accurate stock consumption records and use the designated shared Google Sheet.
Record quantities in pieces/numbers or bottles, not boxes, wherever the sheet requires individual units.
Maintain proper stock storage, expiry-date records, and near-expiry stock monitoring.
Do not make unauthorized stock adjustments or changes in Zoho.
Email Zoho Inventory ID, password or stock discrepancy issues to Aditya (adityakumar.chd@gleuhr.com), copying the RH.
Do not transfer stock between branches without the required management approval and documentation.
Ensure stock received is verified against the relevant documentation and applicable acceptance controls.
4. Physical stock audit and verification
Conduct a complete physical stock count at the branch.
Match physical quantities against the available stock records.
Record product quantities and expiry dates accurately.
Clearly mention every discrepancy instead of adjusting figures to force a match.
Share the completed physical stock audit report with Operations within the announced deadline.
Keep supporting records available for RH and HO verification.
Latest communicated deadline: The physical stock audit report was requested by 22 October 2026.
5. Daily BM EOD report and accountability
Fill and submit the BM EOD Report daily without fail.
Update all required operational fields accurately and on time.
Record visits, revisits, packages, sessions, complaints, attendance, and other required branch performance details.
Record attendance issues, including late arrivals and relevant time deviations, as required by the tracker.
Ensure patient follow-ups and next-appointment details are updated.
Report operational concerns in both the designated tracker and the BM EOD report.
Ensure all open issues have a responsible owner, target resolution date, and follow-up status.
Follow up on pending complaints and operational gaps with the RH until closure.
Respond to operational emails and requests promptly.
Maintain accurate records; do not make backdated or incomplete entries.
Reporting rule: The daily stock report and BM EOD report are separate requirements. Both must be completed every day.
6. Issue tracker and escalation process
Record every operational concern in the designated Issue Tracker.
Raise every issue by email to the POC who owns it, with all related POCs and the RH copied (see Points of contact).
Email operations and maintenance concerns to Saurabh Dixit (saurabhdixit.chd@gleuhr.com).
Provide a clear description of the problem, branch name, responsible person, and required action.
Update the tracker until the concern is resolved.
Share closure evidence wherever applicable.
Escalate critical issues such as machine breakdowns, security incidents, infrastructure failures, and patient-safety concerns without delay.
Do not consider an issue closed merely because it has been reported; closure and resolution must be tracked.
7. Medical and product stock requisition process
The communicated monthly stock-intent schedule must be followed strictly.
1st & 15th
Monthly
Reminder and planning
Review stock availability, consumption, and upcoming requirements.
3rd–5th
Cycle 1
First stock-intent window
Enter Medical and Product requirements in the shared Google Sheet after checking existing stock and consumption.
16th–18th
Cycle 2
Second stock-intent window
Submit the next cycle's requirements using the same verification and approval process.
Additional controls:
Enter the request date and complete the prescribed pre-checks.
Email the RH for approval, copying Aditya (Inventory and Logistics, adityakumar.chd@gleuhr.com), Deepa, the concerned ME, Operations, and upper management as required by the communicated process.
Do not treat a stock request as approved until the RH approves it.
Allow approximately 4–5 days for logistics.
Plan requirements in advance and avoid deviations from the submission windows.
Follow up on pending approvals and missing entries before the deadline.
The communicated fulfillment targets are by the 10th and 22nd of each month, respectively.
8. Petty cash management
The BM petty-cash process requires complete documentation and approval.
Requirement
Process
Weekly allocation
₹4,000
Expense above ₹500
Prior RH approval; payment processed by Deepa
Emergency expense of ₹500
RH approval and Deepa's update required
Early replenishment
May be requested when the balance falls below ₹1,000
Submission deadline
Tuesday evening
Reconciliation
Thursday
Payment target
By Friday
BM responsibilities:
Record every petty-cash transaction in Airtable.
Attach bills, vouchers, or relevant screenshots for every expense.
Mention the name, contact details, amount, purpose, and required signature.
Submit the complete expense details by Tuesday evening.
Ensure the RH verifies the submission before it is forwarded to Deepa with the required recipients copied.
Reconcile the full balance and previous expenditure before requesting the next ₹4,000.
Do not split expenses or bypass the approval process.
9. Patient records, Airtable and CRM compliance
Complete Airtable entries on the same day.
Enter every visit with correct client name, mobile number, treatment, doctor and next appointment, so the doctor and the Feedback Team can call every client within 24 hours (see Client calls within 24 hours).
Select the correct patient status: Visit Done, No Show, Cancelled, or Rescheduled.
Enter the correct customer type and clinic name.
Record the correct payment mode and amount.
Avoid duplicate or unnecessary old entries.
For an old client registered under a new entry, follow the communicated clinic-card photo verification process.
Ensure Reception and Counselors coordinate to maintain accurate patient records.
Follow the prescribed CRM process for token payments, customized plans, package conversion, and complimentary products.
Ensure complimentary products are billed and recorded as instructed, including the ₹1 billing requirement where applicable.
Ensure courier or pickup details are recorded through the prescribed CRM/Airtable workflow.
Ensure prescriptions are entered through the mandatory prescription portal.
Maintain therapist checklists and the required supporting photographs.
10. Day-end financial reconciliation — CRM enhancement requirements
The following are CRM changes requested for development, not confirmation that every feature is already live.
Reconcile Cash, Card, and UPI collections against system-recorded sales.
Capture separate As per Sale and As per Actual amounts.
Ensure reconciliation access for the concerned Accounts Person at both outlet and HO levels.
Enter cash denomination-wise, including ₹500, ₹200, ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes, with quantities.
Automatically calculate the cash total and discrepancy.
Require an explanation for every variance.
Attach a photograph of the sealed cash envelope with the amount, date, and sign-off clearly mentioned.
Attach the card machine day-end transaction slip and the cash reconciliation summary photo.
Block day-end closure if mandatory fields or supporting attachments are missing.
Route discrepancies to the Accounts Head and RH for approval.
Send the day-end reconciliation summary and relevant supporting documents to top management through the proposed automated email workflow.
Additional requested control: If a discrepancy remains unresolved, the next day's collection workflow for the concerned branch should remain blocked until both the Accounts Head and RH confirm approval in the CRM. This restriction is part of the requested development specification and should be confirmed with the CRM/Tech team before being treated as operational policy.
11. G-Money portal and client EMI facility
Inform eligible clients about the available Easy No-Cost EMI option.
Ensure Counselors and Reception staff know the G-Money portal process.
Use the assigned portal credentials and enter accurate client information.
Complete the required application and documentation.
Explain the available EMI tenure, applicable terms, and charges to the client before proceeding.
Do not promise approval until G-Money confirms it.
Verify the transaction status and maintain the required records.
Escalate portal access or processing issues to the concerned support team.
12. Machine, equipment and infrastructure maintenance
Check machine availability and operational status.
Report machine faults promptly and coordinate with the technician.
Complete troubleshooting with the technician before arranging external repairs, where appropriate.
Track machines sent for repair, dispatch details, expected return dates, and closure.
Report CCTV, camera recording, laptop, inverter, lift, electrical, and other infrastructure issues.
Maintain a machine tracker with one entry per machine, including make/company and serial number from the back of the machine, or mark NA where unavailable.
Ensure critical breakdowns have an assigned owner and are followed up daily until resolved.
Do not assume that a reported repair is complete until the machine or equipment has been checked.
Recent examples of reported work included the Karnal diode machine requiring repair, Ahmedabad machine and camera-memory-card issues, and the Amritsar HydraFacial machine request.
13. Security and CCTV controls
Ensure CCTV recording remains active at all times.
Handle the camera application carefully to avoid accidentally stopping or disabling recordings.
Verify that the recording is active after accessing the application.
Immediately escalate any interruption, camera fault, or security concern.
Maintain security-related incident documentation and follow up on corrective actions.
Ensure designated security equipment, lockers, and other approved controls are maintained as applicable to the branch.
14. Staff management, grooming and roster
Maintain correct daily attendance and ensure staff report on time.
Prepare and share the weekly roster, including Sunday coverage, as instructed.
Ensure all staff understand their duties and reporting responsibilities.
Monitor grooming, formal attire, badges, and overall staff presentation.
Email HR and asset matters (attendance, staffing shortages, replacements, staff concerns, branch asset records) to Mizraem (mizraem@gleuhr.com), copying the RH.
Ensure Reception, Housekeeping, Counselors, Therapists, and Doctors complete their respective daily responsibilities.
Ensure required training is completed and credentials are shared with the concerned staff.
Before a new process goes live, confirm that the concerned team understands the step-by-step workflow and can access the required system.
15. Patient experience, complaints and service quality
Monitor patient complaints and feedback.
Coordinate with Doctors, Therapists, Reception, Counselors, and the Feedback Team to resolve concerns.
Email client experience concerns and complaints to Dr Navreet (drnavreet@gleuhr.com), and treatment-result concerns to Dr Kanikta (drkanikta@gleuhr.com), with the RH copied.
Make sure every client is reachable for the doctor’s and the Feedback Team’s calls within 24 hours of each visit.
Track each complaint until closure.
Ensure patient follow-ups and next appointments are updated.
Review treatment and reception feedback trends with the RH.
Escalate serious patient concerns and service failures immediately.
Maintain accurate patient journey and service records wherever required.
16. Coordination with the Regional Head and Operations Team
Contact the assigned RH for regional coordination and support.
Share required reports and updates within the prescribed deadlines.
Ensure the RH has visibility of stock, operational issues, machine breakdowns, complaints, and audit observations.
Cooperate during RH branch visits and audits.
Implement corrective actions arising from audits or management instructions.
Keep trackers updated and provide evidence of resolution.
Follow the designated escalation process for unresolved operational concerns.

18. Non-negotiable operating principles
No missed daily reporting: Stock reports and BM EOD reports must be completed daily.
No unreported operational issues: Log issues in the tracker and follow up until closure.
No unauthorized stock adjustments: Follow the approval and documentation process.
No incomplete financial records: Enter actual collections and retain supporting documents.
No missed audit deadlines: Submit accurate stock counts, quantities, expiry dates, and discrepancies on time.
No unattended maintenance concerns: Assign responsibility and track repair completion.
No lapse in CCTV recording: Protect continuity of security recordings.
No incomplete patient records: Ensure Airtable, CRM, prescription, billing, and follow-up entries are accurate.
No bypassing approvals: Follow the applicable RH, Accounts, and management approval processes.
No closure without evidence: Operational and audit issues must be tracked to verified resolution.
No missed client details: Every visit is entered correctly the same day so every client gets the doctor’s and the Feedback Team’s call within 24 hours.
No issue off email: Every concern goes by email to the right POC with all related POCs in the loop.
